newsitem.title: THAILAND: Weaker economy raised Siam City coupon.
newsitem.headline: Weaker economy raised Siam City coupon.

text.p: Siam City Bank Plc faced a higher than expected funding cost for its $115 million Eurobond issue after lead underwriter JP Morgan Securities advised it to raise its coupon by 15 basis points this month.

Siam City's assistant vice president Ekapong Rugrien said Thai political uncertainty and economic slowdown this year forced the bank to raise the premium on its five-year issue to 100 basis points above US Treasury notes from an earlier planned 85 points.
He said unfavourable Thai economic factors also prompted the bank to postpone indefinitely a separate $120 million Euro convertible debenture planned for this year.
Ekapong said the bank was happy that its Eurobond issue was fully subscribed given Thailand's current domestic economic climate.

He said a protracted slump in the Thai equity market this year and a recent downgrade of Thai short term debt by Moody's Investors Service gave Thai borrowers a tougher time to tap the Euro debt market.

Ekapong said proceeds from its Eurobond issue will be used for Siam City's working capital and for helping it meet a 20 percent lending growth target this year. He said the $115 million raised by the issue would be swapped into Thai baht later this month.
The bank official said Siam City is still committed to a plan to float $1 billion global medium-term note arranged since last October by SBC Warburg.
Siam City earlier issued $100 million worth of floating rate notes in February.
He said the bank plans to float 4.35 billion baht ($174 million) of warrant-attached debentures later this year to raise funds for its second tier capital requirement.
